text:
I am not Jewish and I have been living in Israel for the past 27 years. My husband is not Jewish according to the Jewish law because his father was Jewish and not his mother. 
I never thought about converting, I am Christian and I sincerely don't care what other people think. 
My son, who came with me to Israel , him being from a previous marriage never had any problems with being a Christian. He went to the army, worked a few years there, and then worked in civilian life, with no problems.
My daughter was born here. Since she was young she knew she wasn't Jewish . She went to school here, from the third grade she went to a gifted class, she participated on many projects and programs for gifted, went to the army and now to the University. 
She is thinking now about a Reform conversion because her boyfriend is Jewish and there is the issue of their children ( if they will get married).
But she never felt different, religion wise, maybe because she was always different, being a gifted child.
We always celebrated Jewish and Christian holidays and were open about our beliefs and everything.
My one and only problem is about where I will be buried. In Ashdod,  where we live, in the cemetery they have this big cement wall that separates the Christian graves from the Jewish ones. I don't know, it always makes me uncomfortable whenever I see it. I know I won't care after I' m dead, but still ...
On a funnier note, when my daughter was 6 years old she asked me whether the Jewish people have Santa Claus and when I said they didn't, she was very disappointed and said she would stay a Christian then 😁.
But all in all, I don't have a problem if she wants to convert, it is her personal choice. Me? Too late for that anyway ...
